title: Why Touchscreens Don't Work With Gloves (But a Sausage Does)
caption: Touchscreens sense your body's electric charge, not pressure. Gloves insulate, but a salty, wet sausage conducts like a finger.
pinned_comment: Ever tried using your phone with gloves on? 👇

lines.text: Gloves don't work on touchscreens. Sausages do.
That's because your screen can't feel pressure at all.
Under the glass is a grid of tiny electrodes holding an electric field.
Your finger is mostly salty water, so it conducts electricity.
When it touches the glass, it pulls a tiny bit of charge from the grid.
A chip spots where the charge changed and knows exactly where you tapped.
Wool and leather don't conduct, so the screen feels nothing.

right.heading: Fact
right.text: It needs a conductor, not force

lines.text: A sausage is salty and wet, just like a finger.
In two thousand ten, during a cold snap in South Korea, people used snack sausages to work their phones.
One report said sales jumped by almost forty percent.
Touchscreen gloves have conductive threads in the fingertips.
And rain on your screen? That's water too, which is why it starts tapping on its own.
So this winter, skip the sausage. Or don't…
